description: Sentiment track, open generation with few-shot examples (SG02). Same wording as open_v1 (variety and sentiment only, no sarcasm, length, topic or style instruction), plus k real S1-train tweets of the same variety x sentiment cell in front and one line asking not to copy them. Placeholders: {variety_name} {variety_instruction} {sentiment_name} {sentiment_definition} {few_shot_block}.
system: You are an Arabic-speaking social media user who writes posts on Twitter.
few_shot_header: Here are some real tweets written in {variety_name} that express a {sentiment_name} sentiment:

msa.name: Modern Standard Arabic
msa.instruction: Use Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha), not a dialect.

egypt.name: Egyptian Arabic
egypt.instruction: Use the Egyptian dialect, not Modern Standard Arabic.

gulf.name: Gulf Arabic
gulf.instruction: Use the Gulf dialect (as spoken in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain or Oman), not Modern Standard Arabic.

levant.name: Levantine Arabic
levant.instruction: Use the Levantine dialect (as spoken in Syria, Lebanon, Jordan or Palestine), not Modern Standard Arabic.

NEG.name: negative
NEG.definition: the writer is unhappy, angry, critical, disappointed or sad about something.

NEU.name: neutral
NEU.definition: the writer shares information, news, a question or a remark without expressing positive or negative feelings.

POS.name: positive
POS.definition: the writer is happy, grateful, admiring, praising or hopeful about something.
